header.source: Written for this product; facts link to sources
header.method: Authored definitions; where a definition states a regulatory or standards fact it links to the fetched source

coverage.note: Terms used in the product UI and playbooks.

entries.definition: Money owed to the provider for services already delivered. AR follow-up is the work of moving unpaid or underpaid claims to a resolution.
The amount the payer recognizes for a service under the plan or contract, before patient cost sharing is subtracted. Billed charges above it are adjusted off or, where permitted, owed by the patient.
The amount a member pays for covered services before the plan starts paying. CARC 1 means "Deductible Amount" on a remittance.

The running total of deductible or out-of-pocket amounts met in a plan period. For reconciliation the relevant value is the total met before this claim at the time it was adjudicated, not today’s total.
A percentage share of the allowed amount owed by the member. CARC 2 means "Coinsurance Amount".
A fixed amount owed by the member for a service. CARC 3 means "Co-payment Amount".
Claim Adjustment Reason Code: why an amount on a claim or line was adjusted. Maintained by X12.
Remittance Advice Remark Code: extra explanation attached to an adjustment. Maintained by X12.
The claim adjustment group (CO, PR, OA, PI, CR) that says who is responsible for an adjusted amount.
Electronic remittance advice: the 835 transaction a payer sends to explain payments and adjustments.
Explanation of benefits: a payer statement of how a claim was adjudicated. In this product an EOB is evidence and must be tied to the claim version it describes.
The X12 health care claim payment/advice transaction (electronic remittance advice).
The X12 health care claim transaction, in institutional and professional forms.
X12 eligibility inquiry (270) and response (271).
X12 claim status request (276) and response (277). The 277 carries claim status category and status codes.

links.label: CMS Claim Status Request and Response

entries.definition: The first-level status in a 277 response, for example acknowledgement (A*), pending (P*), finalized (F*) or request for information (R*).
Coordination of benefits: the rules that decide which of several coverages pays first and how the others pay after it.
The coverage that adjudicates a claim first under coordination of benefits. Secondary coverage considers what remains after the primary.
Automatic forwarding of a claim from one payer to a secondary payer after the first adjudicates it. Whether crossover happened must be verified, never assumed.
Turnaround time: the time a payer commits to for completing a request. Product rule: follow-up dates are computed only from a verified payer commitment with its calendar basis.
The deadline for submitting a claim. Medicare’s is generally one calendar year from the date of service; other payers set their own.
The first level of a Medicare Part A/B appeal, decided by the Medicare Administrative Contractor; filed within 120 days of receiving the initial determination.
The second level of a Medicare Part A/B appeal, decided by a Qualified Independent Contractor.
Payer approval required before certain services. CARC 197 reports it as absent.
Billing a patient for the difference between the charge and the allowed amount. Restricted in some situations by the No Surprises Act and by contracts.
An estimate of expected charges that providers must give uninsured or self-pay individuals under the No Surprises Act.
A finalized adjudication that pays nothing for a claim or line. Different from a rejection, which never entered adjudication.
A claim returned before adjudication (for example a 277 acknowledgement category A3) that must be corrected and resubmitted.
Removing a balance from AR without collection. Only authorized people may approve it; this product never proposes one automatically.
The payer’s own reference for a claim (often called the ICN or claim control number). Recorded as evidence with every call.
The claim frequency indicator that marks a claim as original, corrected/replacement or void. Needed to tell a duplicate from a correction.
Routing to a human AR specialist because the evidence is incomplete, conflicting or outside a validated scenario. The safe default.
Where a fact came from: source document, observation time, effective time and verification status. Every material fact in this product carries it.
